item.text: {"verdicts":[{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0004-E001","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0004-E002","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0004-E003","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0004-E004","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0004-E005","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0004-E006","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0004-E007","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0004-E008","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"Amnesty International’s April 2023 submission for Bangladesh’s November 2023 UPR considered excessive police force to curb protests, an expanding state crackdown on dissent, shrinking civic space, impunity for enforced disappearances and extrajudicial killings, marginalization of religious and ethnic minorities and Indigenous peoples, the retention of the death penalty, and climate-change impacts affecting rights and freedoms.","notes":["The excerpt says the submission considers the prohibition of torture; it does not specifically state that it cited torture as an established finding."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0004-E009","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]}]}
